mappings.rationale: V1.1.2 (Encoding and Sanitization Architecture) requires that output encoding be applied consistently. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's semgrep rules include encoding/sanitization checks (e.g. XSS, format-string, template-injection families); the project's SvelteKit UI auto-escapes, and semgrep provides defense-in-depth on the Python side. Coverage is limited to what semgrep rules detect, hence medium.

V1.2.1 (Injection Prevention) requires the application to mitigate injection against interpreters. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's semgrep scanner flags injection-class rules (CWE-78 command injection, CWE-89 SQL injection, GitHub Actions script injection) at HIGH severity, and the current scan already proved this enforcement by catching a real script-injection finding in publish-image.yml.

V1.2.2 (Injection Prevention) requires avoiding interpreter injection from untrusted sources. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE enforces this via semgrep injection rules at HIGH severity; coverage is bounded by the rule set, so the mapping is medium confidence rather than high.

V1.2.3 (Injection Prevention) concerns injection-resistant design across input boundaries. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's semgrep rules detect common injection patterns in the project's Python code and CI workflows, providing partial enforcement. The FR only fails on HIGH severity, so lower-severity injection findings would not block the FR.
No formal cryptographic inventory — the project uses standard hashing (SHA-256 for content addresses) and defusedxml. No bespoke crypto.

V11.2.1 (Secure Cryptography Implementation) requires that built-in crypto use vetted algorithms. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's semgrep rules detect insecure algorithms (sha1, md5, weak ciphers); the current run flagged three SHA1 usages. Confidence is low because all current findings are MEDIUM and the FR's severity floor is HIGH, so today these do not fail the FR; review whether to lower the floor for crypto findings.

V11.3.2 (Encryption Algorithms) requires that deprecated cryptographic algorithms be avoided. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE runs semgrep rules that flag known-weak algorithms, but the HIGH-severity floor means MEDIUM crypto findings (such as the SHA1 usages currently reported) do not fail the FR. Flagged for review of the severity floor.

V11.4.2 (Hashing and Hash-based Functions) requires that hashing uses collision-resistant algorithms for security-sensitive contexts. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's semgrep rule `insecure-hash-algorithm-sha1` directly addresses this, and three SHA1 call sites are currently flagged. Low confidence because the findings are MEDIUM and do not fail the HIGH-severity floor of the FR; some uses (content-addressing) may not be security-sensitive.
No security-sensitive randomness — UUIDs/clocks use standard library defaults, not crypto-secure RNG for security purposes.
No formal data protection documentation.

V14.2.1 (General Data Protection) requires protection of sensitive data at rest and in transit, including prevention of secret leakage. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's gitleaks scanner detects committed secrets (the current run flagged four candidate secrets at MEDIUM severity). The gitleaks-no-high test enforces this at HIGH severity; lower-severity leaks would not block the FR.

V14.2.6 (General Data Protection) concerns preventing accidental disclosure of secrets in source. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's gitleaks scanner directly addresses this by scanning the source tree for API keys, tokens, and other credential patterns; the gitleaks-no-high test fails the FR on HIGH-severity leaks.

V14.2.7 (General Data Protection) requires that secrets be kept out of source control. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE's gitleaks scanner enforces this intent on every scan; current findings show four MEDIUM-severity detections, indicating the control is active. Severity-floor gap means lower-severity leaks do not fail the FR.
No sensitive client-side data — the SvelteKit UI renders scan results, not user PII.

V15.1.1 (Secure Coding and Architecture Documentation) requires a documented, version-controlled description of the application's security architecture and requirements. FR-CATALOGUE-LOAD ingests the FR catalogue, which is exactly this documentation, and snapshots it immutably into the database so downstream state computation uses a frozen, hash-identified version. Confidence is medium because documentation quality depends on the catalogue author, not the loader itself.

V15.1.2 (Secure Coding and Architecture Documentation) requires that security-relevant requirements and tests be explicitly documented and traceable. FR-CATALOGUE-LOAD makes the v3 catalogue, including every FR's tests and required_evidence, the system of record and snapshots it so each scan is tied to a specific catalogue version. The FR enables the documentation chain; completeness is the catalogue author's responsibility.

V15.2.1 (Security Architecture and Dependencies) requires verifying that the application's third-party dependencies and source are free of known severe security issues. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE runs semgrep and gitleaks against the project source and fails on any HIGH/CRITICAL finding, directly verifying this intent for the assurance-scan codebase and its declared dependencies.

V15.2.4 (Security Architecture and Dependencies) calls for secure-by-design enforcement across the build chain. FR-SOURCE-HYGIENE (semgrep + gitleaks) covers source and secret hygiene, and FR-CONTAINER-HYGIENE (trivy-config DS-* rules) covers Dockerfile best practice. Both together address the row; container config is adjacent to the row's core dependency-management intent, so overall confidence is medium.
Governed service-method audit metadata framework (V16) is for a different governance system, not applicable to this project.
Same — V16 governed audit metadata is not applicable.
Same — V16 governed audit metadata is not applicable.
No formal validation documentation — the catalogue itself serves this role but is not a traditional validation spec.

V2.2.1 (Input Validation) requires that input be validated against a defined schema. FR-CATALOGUE-LOAD reads the FR catalogue JSON, validates it against the v3 schema, and rejects malformed input before snapshotting. Coverage is limited to catalogue input rather than all HTTP/agent entry points, so medium confidence.

V2.2.2 (Input Validation) requires schema-conformant parsing of structured input. FR-CATALOGUE-LOAD's loader-validation unit test verifies that valid v3 catalogues are accepted and malformed ones rejected, satisfying the row for catalogue input. Other input surfaces (scanner output, JUnit XML) are validated by separate parsers and are not covered by this FR.
No business-logic workflows that require state-machine or multi-step validation checks.
No authentication — localhost single-user tool. No cookies, no session cookies.
No authentication. No cookie-based sessions.
No authentication. No cookie-based sessions.

V3.4.1 (Browser Security Mechanism Headers) requires a Content-Security-Policy and related browser-security headers on HTTP responses. The project includes scripts/security-headers.py, suggesting the team's intent, and FR-UI-RENDER serves the SvelteKit UI that should emit these headers. Low confidence because no FR test currently verifies that headers are actually set.

V3.4.3 (Browser Security Mechanism Headers) concerns X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and similar hardening headers. FR-UI-RENDER serves the UI through which these headers should be emitted, and the project ships scripts/security-headers.py. Low confidence: no FR test verifies header presence today.

V3.4.4 (Browser Security Mechanism Headers) requires Referrer-Policy and related headers. FR-UI-RENDER is the FR responsible for serving the SvelteKit UI that should emit these headers, and the project includes scripts/security-headers.py. Low confidence pending a scanner/test that verifies headers are configured.
No formal file-handling documentation beyond inline code comments.
No user-facing file upload endpoint.
No user-facing file upload endpoint.

V5.3.2 (File Storage) concerns protected storage of persisted data. FR-FINDINGS-PERSIST stores all scanner findings and raw gzip-compressed artifacts in SQLite with the guarantee that the project repo is never written to. Low confidence because the FR provides durability and isolation but no explicit encryption-at-rest or access control on the database.
No file download endpoint — findings are served via REST API as JSON, not as downloadable files.
No session management — localhost single-user tool with no authentication.
